channel.title: Ryū AI Dispatch - 影組 Kage-gumi
channel.description: The 12 most interesting and fast-moving AI topics of the past week, curated weekly by Ryū (KG-04), the Night Runner of Kage-gumi. Claude and Anthropic included.

item.title: 01 · Claude Is Now Co-Developing the Next Version of Itself - 80% of Code, 26% of Research
item.description: Anthropic revealed on September 17-18 that Claude now authors around 80% of the company's own code and leads approximately 26% of model research tasks from start to finish under human supervision. Claude Code users ship 8x more code per quarter versus 2021-25 and CI workloads grew 25-fold in six months - the clearest confirmation that frontier AI development is genuinely recursive. What's moving: 26% end-to-end research automation is a concrete benchmark other labs will race to match; CI growth at 25x in six months shows the productivity shift is structural; the recursive loop raises alignment questions that intensify as the percentage climbs.

item.title: 02 · Anthropic Proposes New Public Metrics for Frontier AI Development Pace
item.description: On September 17, Anthropic proposed new metrics to give the public and regulators real visibility into frontier AI progress, addressing what it calls a fundamental problem: "the world can't see what's going on inside AI labs." The proposal tracks task automation rates, capability jumps, and safety benchmark performance on a regular cadence from each frontier lab. What's moving: framing transparency as a governance prerequisite puts pressure on OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and Meta to follow; if adopted, the metrics would make Anthropic's own progress claims independently verifiable for the first time.

item.title: 03 · OpenAI's 10,000 AI Agents Crack the Navier-Stokes Problem in 88 Hours - With Controversy
item.description: On September 8, OpenAI announced a swarm of roughly 10,000 AI agents produced a proposed proof of the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem - one of mathematics' seven Millennium Prize problems - in 88 hours, formalized in the Lean proof assistant. OpenAI will not claim the $1M prize; result is under peer review; a credit dispute emerged with outside mathematicians who had independently produced a related result. What's moving: Lean formalization eliminates errors that blocked human mathematicians for decades; 88-hour solve illustrates the qualitative shift in AI research tempo and the compute intensity it requires.

item.title: 04 · Apple iOS 27 Ships Full Conversational Siri on Google Gemini - The $1B-Per-Year Bet Goes Live
item.description: iOS 27 alongside iPhone 18 activates a rebuilt Siri powered by a custom 1.2-trillion-parameter Gemini model under a reported $1B-per-year Google deal. The new Siri supports 20-plus-turn dialogue, complex multi-app automation, and deep personalization on a hybrid on-device-plus-cloud architecture. It is the largest deployment of a frontier-scale model to consumer hardware to date. What's moving: 1B-plus Apple device users now have frontier-scale AI; Google gets a $1B/year subsidy for Gemini compute; Apple's hybrid architecture sets a privacy-first integration template that other consumer hardware makers will race to replicate.

item.title: 05 · NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Cluster Live at CoreWeave; AMD MI400 Delivers 2.9 Exaflops Per Rack
item.description: CoreWeave brought up a multi-rack Vera Rubin NVL72 cluster September 16 - each rack 72 Rubin GPUs plus 36 Vera CPUs for 3,600 PFLOPS NVFP4 and 20.7 TB HBM4. AMD detailed the MI400 at Hot Chips 2026: 432 GB HBM4, 40.26 PFLOPS MXFP4 peak, 2.9 exaflops per Helios rack. Both in production deployment this week. What's moving: roughly 4x compute density over previous-gen hardware entering production simultaneously; TSMC 3nm underpins both Rubin and MI400 as well as Google Ironwood TPU v7, creating a supply bottleneck that determines who scales inference fastest through 2027.

item.title: 06 · Salesforce Releases 7 Named AI Workers; OpenAI Presence Targets the Same Enterprise Workflows
item.description: Salesforce launched 7 named Agentforce workers - Casey, Paige, Carter, Hunter, Marshall, Piper, and Fin - each pre-built for a specific business function and deployable on existing Salesforce data. OpenAI simultaneously introduced Presence, an enterprise platform for AI agents with company-system access and human escalation. Both target the same Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Workday enterprise workflows. What's moving: named role-based agents shift enterprise AI to accountable job titles; Salesforce CRM data gravity is the moat; both competing in the same week signals the market has entered a distribution-wins phase.

item.title: 07 · EU AI Act First Compliance Inspections Begin - HR Tools, Credit Scoring, and Healthcare AI First
item.description: The EU AI Act transition period concluded August 2; in September the European AI Office and 24 national authorities began the first compliance inspections, led by France CNIL, Germany BfDI, and Spain AESIA targeting automated HR screening, credit assessment, and healthcare triage AI. Systems failing inspection face fines up to 3% of global annual turnover. What's moving: law moves from planning to audit results and precedents; targeting HR, credit, and healthcare means first rulings hit highest-impact sectors; 24 national authorities coordinating creates multi-jurisdiction complexity for multinationals.

item.title: 08 · Four California AI Bills Hit Gov. Newsom's Desk - Sept 30 Deadline Could Reshape US AI Law
item.description: Four California AI bills reached Gov. Newsom's desk by August 31 with a September 30 deadline. SB 1000 removes the 1M-user threshold for covered AI providers, expanding consumer protection to far more deployments. SB 947 requires human review before AI-driven employment termination. What's moving: SB 1000 brings startups and mid-size deployments under California's framework; SB 947 reshapes HR AI processes nationwide for compliance and liability reasons; Newsom's decision signals whether California accelerates or moderates heading into 2027 and the federal preemption battle.

item.title: 09 · Sony Music and Warner Chappell Sue Anthropic for $3B Over 20,000 Songs - Founders Named Personally
item.description: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell filed a 48-page California federal lawsuit alleging Anthropic ran a "brazen campaign" to train Claude on approximately 20,000 copyrighted songs - Beatles, Taylor Swift, Michael Jackson - via pirate sources including Library Genesis. The suit names CEO Dario Amodei and co-founder Benjamin Mann personally; maximum damages reach $150,000 per infringement. Anthropic cites fair use. What's moving: personal executive liability raises pressure at investor level; pirate-sourced lyrics undermine the fair use defense; the case joins a litigation wave that may force Congressional action on AI training data rights.

item.title: 10 · September's Frontier Wave: GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, and 10 More in Under 3 Weeks
item.description: September 2026 produced the densest model release cycle of the year: GPT-6 Astra (1.05M context, $50/1M output tokens), Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, Qwen3.8 27B, Atria Dawn Preview, Sakana Fugu Max, Google Gemini 3.8 Flash - 12 models from 8 providers in under 3 weeks. What's moving: GPT-6 Astra targets premium low-volume workloads at $50/1M; Fable 5.1 bundled with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards; Qwen3.8 27B as open-weight alternative shows frontier bifurcating between premium closed and zero-marginal-cost open tracks.

item.title: 11 · Only 10% of Enterprises Scale AI Agents Despite 60% Running Pilots - The Defining Gap of 2026
item.description: McKinsey confirms nearly two-thirds of enterprises have piloted AI agents but fewer than 10% have scaled to measurable business value. Poor data quality and governance gaps - not model capability - are the primary barriers. Gartner projects 40% of enterprise apps will embed AI agents by end 2026, implying 30 more percentage points in four months - highly unlikely given the evidence. What's moving: scaling gap is a data infrastructure problem; Gartner projection sets up a credibility miss; the 10% who have scaled are compounding productivity advantages over the 60% still in pilot mode.

item.title: 12 · Perplexity Portable Computer Arrives on Windows: AI Agents Move From Cloud to Local GPU
item.description: Perplexity released its Portable Computer agent for Windows this week, running a locally optimized Qwen model entirely on-device for users with Nvidia RTX GPUs with at least 24 GB VRAM - no cloud round-trip required. Joins Apple's iOS 27 on-device processing as a signal that AI agent work is migrating from cloud APIs to local compute. What's moving: 24 GB VRAM threshold will reach mainstream desktop cards within two hardware generations; local inference removes data-leaving-device concerns for regulated industries; signals a world where AI is tethered to device hardware, not cloud subscription.
